inputs.text: The court’s finding that Mary Ngechi Ngethe played a central role in the purchase of unsuitable cemetery land for Ksh.283 million is a warning about a system where weak oversight lets public money serve insiders rather than communities. When essential services are compromised, people with the least power to challenge officials bear the greatest cost. Holding individuals accountable matters, but lasting change means reforming procurement and oversight so public resources are directed toward public needs.
